claims.title: Mitochondrial cycles reverse at zero free energy and dissipate power in either direction
claims.statement: Each enabled mitochondrial cycle runs forward at negative full-turn ΔG, reverses at positive ΔG and stalls at zero. The five electrogenic cycles have a stall voltage set by free activities. Phosphate uptake and K⁺/H⁺ exchange have voltage-independent stall ratios. At positive temperature, instantaneous dissipated power is positive in either direction and vanishes exactly at stall or when the population is off.
assumptions: Each reaction uses the declared free species and signed charge, with N the matrix and P the intermembrane space. Free activities are positive. The dimensionless voltage is F(φ_N − φ_P)/(RT).
An enabled population has a positive finite forward kinetic prefactor. Complex III uses a half-turn exponent and complex IV a quarter-turn exponent. ΔG refers to a full turnover in both cases.
Heat here is the model's instantaneous chemical free-energy dissipation. Flux is in fmol/s and RT in J/mol. An assay of integrated whole-mitochondrion enthalpy measures a different observable.

numerical.result: All 49 physical settings agreed with the independent component equations on NumPy and compiled CPU JAX, including both sides of stall for all seven laws. The worst net-flux error was 3.91 × 10⁻¹⁴ of the reference forward rate. The worst residual ΔG/(RT) at a calculated stall was 2.85 × 10⁻¹⁴. The rate kernel also preserved the signs at ±2⁻⁶⁰ and returned zero at an exact zero input. The probe and the stage agreed on flux and instantaneous dissipated power.

biology.observable: Net turnover on either side of a measured mitochondrial stall, the shift in ATP synthase stall with phosphorylation load, and dissipated power at known cycle affinity.
biology.unit: turnovers per enzyme per second, pH units, H⁺/ATP, pJ/s per population

evidence.citation: Petersen et al. (2012), Figs. 1–4 and Tables S2 and S4
evidence.locator: Yeast traces in Fig. 1, corrected stall in Fig. 2, fitted coupling in Fig. 4 and all ten corrected stall entries in Table S4.
evidence.context: Purified yeast mitochondrial ATP synthase in proteoliposomes at an imposed 60 mV.
evidence.uncertainty: The example rates are fitted initial slopes. The equilibrium ΔpH was interpolated. One measured stall sets the offset for comparing shifts at the other loads. The comparison adds the reported interpolation limits and assumes the assay's concentration quotient is proportional to the free activity quotient.
evidence.assessment: ATP turnover changed sign across stall, and the inferred coupling was 2.9 ± 0.2 H⁺/ATP. The model's three protons predict a 0.745 pH-unit endpoint shift against 0.74 observed. Five of nine other entries are within the combined interpolation limits using the stall at Q = 5.79 as the reference. Four intermediate entries fall outside.

evidence.locator: The anaerobic bulk heat pulse in Fig. 5b and its dependence on the initial ADP in Fig. 6.
evidence.context: Rat liver mitochondria following aerobic ATP production and oxygen exhaustion.
evidence.uncertainty: The apparent enthalpy was −29 ± 7 kJ per mole of previously added ADP. The authors inferred an ATP hydrolysis contribution.
evidence.assessment: Bulk calorimetry integrates heat from the preparation. The instantaneous dissipated power of each individual mitochondrial cycle remains experimentally open.

claims.title: Restoring both respiratory carriers fixes the turnover ratio and outward charge
claims.statement: For signed extents of mitochondrial complexes I, III and IV, restoring reduced quinone and reduced cytochrome c fixes their turnover in the ratio 2:2:1. Two NADH and one oxygen then give twenty outward charge equivalents, with every intermediate redox carrier restored.
assumptions: N is the matrix and P the intermembrane space. The tracked species use the registered base forms, with explicit protons. Water is implicit.
The complete-chain ratio assumes no other source or sink for the two intermediate carriers. The per-cycle identities hold for arbitrary signed extents, including a transient.

numerical.result: All seven registered columns were checked against independently written material balances. Per forward turnover the respiratory complexes added 4, 2 and 8 net charges on P, while each added four explicit P protons. In two checked steps of a finite-matrix/lumen world, the redox, adenine and phosphate changes matched predictions from the measured extents within 8.28 × 10⁻²⁵ fmol.

biology.observable: Protons transported per NADH, including correction for proton consumption by quinone reduction, and net charge transport during a carrier-balanced respiratory sequence.
biology.unit: H⁺ per NADH or two electrons, charge equivalents per O₂

evidence.citation: Galkin et al. (1999), Fig. 2 and Eq. 3
evidence.locator: Fig. 2, right panel, and the scalar-proton correction in Eq. 3.
evidence.context: NADH-driven quinone reduction in inside-out bovine heart submitochondrial particles.
evidence.uncertainty: The authors report 4.00 ± 0.05, estimated from initial rates after correcting for one proton consumed by quinone reduction.
evidence.assessment: The observed 4.00 ± 0.05 transported protons per two electrons agrees with the four on P per forward complex I turnover. The full three-complex charge balance needs additional measurements.

evidence.citation: Jones et al. (2017), Table 3 and Fig. 3
evidence.locator: Bovine estimates in Table 3 derived from the paired flux measurements in Fig. 3.
evidence.context: Four bovine heart submitochondrial preparations. The three comparisons match ATP synthesis rates to approximate equal proton leak.
evidence.uncertainty: Reported propagated errors. All three comparisons use the same four preparations.
evidence.assessment: The estimates were 4.21 ± 0.15, 4.10 ± 0.17 and 4.02 ± 0.19 H⁺/2e⁻. They support a value near four for complex I. They do not directly measure the three-complex net charge.

claims.title: ATP synthesis and delivery return four charge equivalents in the declared three-proton model
claims.statement: One ATP synthesis, nucleotide exchange and phosphate import restore the matrix ATP, ADP and phosphate rows and deliver one ATP on P. Their net P-side charge is −4. Potassium–proton exchange swaps one K for one H with zero net charge. At balanced respiratory carriers and zero net charge transfer the seven paths imply five ATP deliveries per oxygen.
assumptions: The registered synthase has three translocated protons per matrix ATP. Nucleotides and phosphate use the declared base forms and all proton rows are explicit.
The five-per-O₂ identity assumes matched turnovers of synthesis, ATP export and phosphate import, and no additional electrogenic paths. It is an ideal stoichiometric ratio.

numerical.result: The synthesized ATP, nucleotide exchange, phosphate import and K/H exchange carry −3, −1, 0 and 0 net charge equivalents on P per turn. All seven populations carried nonzero extents in two checked 1 ms steps. The independently calculated combined material postings matched the engine ledger. Global charge error stayed below 1.0 × 10⁻³³ C.

biology.observable: Rotor proton count and ATP turnover for synthesis, plus the energetic cost of delivering ATP across the mitochondrial inner membrane.
biology.unit: c-subunits per rotor, H⁺ per matrix ATP, charge equivalents per delivered ATP

evidence.citation: Watt et al. (2010), Fig. 1 and Discussion
evidence.locator: The bovine c-ring in Fig. 1 and the authors' coupling interpretation.
evidence.context: Structure of the bovine mitochondrial F1–c-ring complex.
evidence.uncertainty: The 3.5 Å structure resolves eight c-subunits. The stoichiometric interpretation assumes tight coupling and three ATP per full rotation.
evidence.assessment: The bovine structure implies 8/3 H⁺ per matrix ATP under tight coupling, and the authors infer 11/3 proton equivalents per delivered ATP. The current Cells model fixes 3 and 4. The structural result identifies a preparation-specific limit of that choice. It does not measure ATP flux under load.

claims.title: Each compartment belongs to one cell and its charge sets its lumen voltage
claims.statement: Summing each cell's cytosol with the compartments it owns counts every species amount once. A lumen with a single bounding capacitor sits above its owner's potential by its net free charge divided by that capacitance.
assumptions: Each finite lumen has exactly one owner and positive bounding capacitance. The voltage formula assumes that its bounding membrane supplies its only capacitor plate.
In the numerical comparison each cell and lumen exchange material externally only with their own held bath.

numerical.result: Two cells and their private lumens balanced every species against the corresponding bath within 4.34 × 10⁻¹⁹ fmol. The trafficking lumen reached +29.83 mV relative to its owner at the end of retrieval. The largest discrepancy from charge divided by capacitance across both lumens was 1.39 × 10⁻¹⁷ V.

biology.observable: Lumen voltage relative to its own cytosol, with whole-compartment free charge and capacitance in the same preparation.

evidence.locator: Resting lysosome measurements in Fig. 4i and the optical calibration in Fig. 4.
evidence.context: Intact HEK293 cells. The experimental convention is lumen minus cytosol. The Cells bounding patch uses the opposite orientation.
evidence.uncertainty: Mean ± SD across seven independent experiments with 106 lysosome regions. The calibration estimates its zero-potential endpoint.
evidence.assessment: Resting lumen potential was +56 ± 7 mV relative to cytosol. This locates the resting voltage in this preparation. The experiment supplies neither net free charge nor capacitance, and the checked generic lumen has no calibrated native transport.

claims.title: Returning membrane area can leave some of its channels in the receiving pool
claims.statement: Retrieval carries away source-specific capacitance and leaves each population proportional to the remaining area fraction raised to its enrichment. Transfers conserve area, capacitance and each channel population. Returning the same area from a seeded, uniformly mixed pool leaves a positive share of the retrieved cohort inside.
assumptions: A positive source area remains after each transfer. Enrichments are nonnegative, constant over the compared stages and refer to the population at its source patch.
The round-trip formula uses uniform retrieval and recycling for the tracked cohort, a positive seed area, no initial internal cohort and no production or removal during the cycle.

numerical.result: A four-step cycle recovered all retrieved area. Of the initial 3,261.27 Kir units, 444.72 (13.64%) stayed in the pool. Two populations followed independent enrichment and recycling predictions within 3.42 × 10⁻¹³ units. The plasma gained 2.224 pF from mixing with a pool of higher specific capacitance. A separate extreme depletion comparison is recorded under empty-surface-flow.

biology.observable: Time-resolved membrane area or capacitance, internal cargo, and surface cargo of the same cohort during retrieval and recycling.
biology.unit: pF and fraction of labelled cargo

evidence.locator: Fig. 5c–d for the snapshot and Fig. 5e for recycling in a separate chase.
evidence.context: Endogenous AMPA receptors in basal primary hippocampal neuronal cultures. The snapshot uses whole-cell label. The chase uses a reference surface signal.
evidence.uncertainty: Mean ± SEM, three biological replicates for each measurement.
evidence.assessment: After 10 h of labelling, 90.4 ± 0.6% of the label was at the surface and 10.3 ± 1.7% was internal. In the 15 min chase, resurfaced label was 12.5 ± 2.8% of the reference surface signal. The missing terminal internal stock prevents a closed recycling balance.

evidence.locator: Fig. 1C–E, peak capacitance and the fractions of capacitance and synaptotagmin-2 fluorescence remaining 60 s after stimulation.
evidence.context: Stimulated calyces of Held in brainstem slices at room temperature. Each readout is normalized to its own peak excess.
evidence.uncertainty: Mean ± SEM across seven capacitance and ten fluorescence recordings. Seven were simultaneous. Fluorescence depends on vesicle re-acidification.
evidence.assessment: After a 1.52 ± 0.21 pF capacitance rise, 0.33 ± 0.06 of peak excess capacitance and 0.47 ± 0.07 of peak fluorescence remained at 60 s. These measurements constrain net retrieval and cargo recovery separately. Absolute internal channel counts remain open.

claims.title: Charge carriers reconcile daughter volume and membrane shares at division
claims.statement: Each species balances across the daughters when charge carriers compensate for the difference between volume-weighted and area-weighted parent charge. Splitting each capacitor and its charge in the same proportion preserves patch voltage. Positive daughter amounts have nonnegative ideal unmixing cost.
assumptions: Volume and active patch shares lie strictly between zero and one. Capacitors are positive. Compensating carrier charge fractions sum to one and each carrier has nonzero valence.
Both daughters have positive amounts and proportional reference volumes. The independent work calculation uses the single-parent fixture with one membrane against a held bath.

numerical.result: For a 75% volume share and a 60% membrane share, K and counterion offsets of +0.001008 and −0.001008 fmol supplied the 1.94515 × 10⁻¹³ C mismatch. At the event, each daughter pair summed to the parent's amount exactly in float64. Daughter voltages agreed with the parent's within 1.39 × 10⁻¹⁷ V. Booked work agreed with a 65-digit unmixing calculation within 1.69 × 10⁻¹⁷ pJ.

biology.observable: Parent and both daughter volumes, ionic amounts, patch areas and potentials immediately across division.

evidence.locator: Supplement p. 4, panel labelled S2L and cited as S2L in the main text.
evidence.context: Eleven paired mouse basal epidermal divisions in vivo. The next image after the mitotic parent gives the sum of both daughters.
evidence.uncertainty: The imaging interval was 12 h. Mean repeat-segmentation difference across the study was 9.1 ± 8.6%.
evidence.assessment: The mean parent volume was 770 µm³ and the mean summed daughter volume in the next image was 677 µm³. The interval includes growth and mitotic volume changes. Instantaneous volume, carrier charge and voltage partition remain open.

claims.title: A closing daughter bridge scales flux by its remaining aperture
claims.statement: Successive intervals compose for capped linear and exponential aperture closure. Linear closure reaches zero at its declared deadline. Exponential closure stays positive at every finite time from a positive starting aperture. The remaining aperture scales the fully open bridge's permeability–area product.
assumptions: Closure is continuously enabled over the tested intervals, with a positive initial aperture and a fixed positive closure time.

The flux comparison evaluates the same concentrations, potentials and gate before and after changing only bridge availability. The single-stalk biological comparison assumes proportionality between stalk diameter and aperture.

numerical.result: After the checked division, both eight-step worlds matched the corresponding analytic aperture. At the 3 ms deadline availability was 0 for linear closure and 0.367879 for exponential closure. Species fluxes agreed with the same-state open flux scaled by analytic aperture within 5.09 × 10⁻²¹ fmol/s.

biology.observable: Bridge diameter and inter-daughter transport during late cytokinesis in the same bridge, including the time and conditions of isolation.
biology.unit: µm, s, nS, normalized tracer exchange per second

evidence.locator: Fig. 1D, microtubule-stalk diameter at the midbody rim in one representative bridge. Fig. 1E relates microtubule loss to membrane closure.
evidence.context: Developing zebrafish embryos. The first plotted frame sets elapsed time. Diameter ratios equal aperture ratios under the proxy assumption.
evidence.uncertainty: The plotted series has no pointwise error bars. The overall series comprised 18 bridges in five embryos. Membrane continuity can outlast tubulin visibility.
evidence.assessment: The held-out diameter at 15 min was about 1.6 µm. The first two readings predicted 0 µm for linear closure and 0.655 µm for exponential closure. Both miss the plateau in this bridge. Actual ionic aperture and variability among bridges remain open.

evidence.locator: Original measurements in section 5. Fig. 2A shows the midbody and 2C reports the conductance distribution.
evidence.context: Dividing HeLa sister pairs with a visible midbody bridge. Conductance was measured across the two daughters.
evidence.uncertainty: Fifteen bridges, with a reported mean of 32 ± 6 nS. The authors do not identify the error statistic. Elapsed time in Fig. 2B follows a recording, and bridge age since furrowing was unreported.
evidence.assessment: Conductance ranged from below 1 to 70 nS. This supplies an electrical scale. The study lacks simultaneous repeated radii for testing conductance as a function of aperture.

evidence.locator: Fig. 4D–E, control dextran exchange slopes, with time measured from furrow ingression.
evidence.context: First division of C. elegans embryos. The observable is 10 kDa dextran exchange normalized by the initial inter-daughter fluorescence difference.
evidence.uncertainty: Approximate graph readings with 90% intervals, about ten slopes per bin and partially overlapping windows.
evidence.assessment: The exchange slope fell from 0.0108/s (0.0085–0.0130) at 30 s to −0.0004/s (−0.0019–0.0011) at 260 s. The late interval includes zero. This establishes loss of measurable tracer exchange without fixing the ionic conductance or its time law.

claims.title: Precursor molecules balance across maturation, surface insertion and removal
claims.statement: Routes on the same precursor and cell share first-order consumption. Weighting each route's functional units by its precursor stoichiometry accounts for molecules in transit, on the surface and in the removal ledger. A two-stage maturation pulse and a surface cohort undergoing first-order loss have explicit time courses.
assumptions: Rates are constant over each interval. Each route has a positive number of precursor molecules per functional unit. Unit amounts evolve continuously. The material identity admits any finite number of sequential maturation pools, including direct insertion.
The pulse starts entirely in the first of two identical stages with no new input or surface removal. The cohort survival comparison tracks labelled surface units with no new labelled insertions.

numerical.result: An eight-step checked world used two precursor molecules per direct unit and seven per three-stage unit. All observed precursor, transit, insertion, surface and sink amounts matched the independent matrix exponential within 4.55 × 10⁻¹³ units and 4.24 × 10⁻²² fmol. In a compiled two-stage pulse, 10.82448 of the initial 120 units reached the membrane in 12.5 ms.

biology.observable: Survival of a labelled surface-channel cohort and appearance of newly made receptors in the plasma membrane.
biology.unit: % of labelled baseline and hours to surface appearance

evidence.locator: Filled circles in Figure 3D, anchored to day 7. Elapsed times and percent retention were read from the point centers and caps.
evidence.context: Ten innervated mouse hindlimbs were followed with the other leg denervated. Residual receptor-associated label is a proxy for survival. The day-7 normalization favors the slower component.
fit: Anchor and seven elapsed days (100% and approximately 67%)
evidence.uncertainty: Readings are approximate. The caption specifies SD and the methods specify SEM. Repeated measures share the animals and baseline.
evidence.assessment: A single rate of 0.05721/day predicted 44.89%, 40.04% and 35.71% retention against 48%, 43% and 42%. The first two predictions fall inside the plotted bars. The last lies below the observed 39–46% bar.

evidence.locator: Abstract observations over the first 3 and 3.5 hours.
evidence.context: Newly synthesized acetylcholine receptors were followed to the plasma membrane in cultured chick skeletal muscle.
evidence.uncertainty: The observations describe relative labelling of receptors arriving at the membrane. The report gives no numerical fraction or error for the 3.5-hour observation.
evidence.assessment: Few labelled receptors reached the surface during the first three hours. By 3.5 hours virtually all receptors entering the membrane carried label. This supports a lag in appearance and leaves the pool count and transit-time distribution open.

claims.title: At fixed channel drive, whole-patch flow tracks the surface unit count
claims.statement: The membrane state converts declared abundance and a signed unit change to a density at the current patch area. Multiplication by area cancels that dilution, so total channel flow scales with the surface unit count at fixed single-channel drive.
assumptions: Patch area and reference density are positive. Capacitance, voltage, concentration difference, permeability and gating are fixed for the flow comparison.
The endplate comparison assumes that available binding-site density is proportional to available functional units across conditions, with comparable effective areas and per-unit driving conditions.

numerical.result: At 1, 1.4 and 1.8 times the declared area, two populations on one patch preserved their potassium fluxes at fixed count. Halving each count halved its flux. The largest relative difference was 4.45 × 10⁻¹⁶ across NumPy and compiled CPU controls.

biology.observable: Peak synaptic-current magnitude at measured available receptor-site densities and whole-patch flow at fixed count as surface area changes.

evidence.locator: Table 1 reports available receptor-site densities and absolute miniature endplate current amplitudes for three conditions.
evidence.context: Esterase-inactivated lizard intercostal endplates were recorded at −100 mV and 23 °C. Density is per µm² of receptor-rich membrane.
fit: Control with 18,000 sites/µm² and 7.5 nA mean peak current
evidence.uncertainty: Estimated standard errors include systematic uncertainties in current and density. The table gives condition means without a biological sample count per row.
evidence.assessment: Scaling by central density gave 3.42 and 2.88 nA against 4.0 ± 0.7 and 2.5 ± 0.5 nA. Both values are within the reported current uncertainties. The measurements leave the functional unit count and the effect of varying area at fixed count open.

claims.title: An empty surface population has zero abundance and channel flow
claims.statement: Removing the full declared number of functional units sets both the normalized abundance and the channel's contribution to zero for any positive patch area. The two-term float64 readout can retain a signed residue.
assumptions: The two initial channel counts are exactly representable, and the state subtracts those counts exactly. The engine accepts the controlled state at each tested area.

The controlled states isolate abundance at fixed capacitance and drive. A second comparison follows a scheduled four-step retrieval from the declared initial state of 3,072 Kir units, with synthetic enrichment 1,024 and a total area decrease of 30%.

numerical.result: Prepared zero-unit states gave potassium flux of −2.19124 × 10⁻¹⁸ and +2.81730 × 10⁻¹⁸ fmol/s at 1.4 and 1.8 times declared area. Scheduled retrieval reached a zero Kir count at 70% of the starting area. At 4 ms its abundance was −2.22045 × 10⁻¹⁶, its potassium flux was −5.58157 × 10⁻¹⁹ fmol/s and the engine refused the observation. The ordinary enrichment and the diagnostic that set abundance to zero at zero count both completed.

biology.observable: The zero-unit case is a numerical identity. Resolving a physiological consequence would require a measurable residual current.

claims.title: Simultaneous replacement books the old and arriving species, charge and electrical work
claims.statement: At each due site the previous occupant leaves and a template or a copy of a pre-event donor enters. Gross supply minus gross removal equals the tissue change for each species. Valence weights give the signed charge. The equal shares of field energy less electrode work sum to one field adjustment.
assumptions: A finite set of tissue sites is replaced simultaneously. Sites outside that set retain their amounts. Copying a donor uses its pre-event amounts, including when that donor is also due.

Field-energy sharing requires at least one due site. Capacitor energy and held-electrode work enter the formal result as signed inputs. The numerical comparison computes each independently for a sheet with one membrane and one held bath per cell.

numerical.result: One cell copied a donor that simultaneously received a template. Gross species transfers, image charge, electrode work and generation replay matched the expected state. The largest per-site free-energy residual was 2.21 × 10⁻¹³ pJ against 2 × 10⁻¹¹ pJ. A three-step checked sheet recorded exactly one exchange at each of the two due sites.

biology.observable: Time between basal-layer exit and compensating local division, and the species amounts in the departing and arriving cells at one site.

evidence.locator: Figure 3C follows neighboring fates after a basal cell differentiates.
evidence.context: Intravital recordings covered two 90 × 90 µm fields of adult mouse epidermis and counted 524 divisions and 529 differentiations.
evidence.uncertainty: The main panel shows one mouse. The 1.8-day estimate is a fitted coordination time scale.
evidence.assessment: Neighboring division followed differentiation on a 1.8-day time scale. Cells takes its schedule as an input. The assay leaves the identity and ion inventory of an immediate same-site arrival open.

claims.title: Replacement over water accounts for incoming volume and composition-dependent free energy
claims.statement: For a donor copy, transfer of the donor's volume increment preserves its physical volume when reference volumes agree. Adding the water term to the chemical energy at the declared volume evaluates all tracked species at the physical volume. A composition change can give nonzero water free energy even at zero net volume transfer.
assumptions: All cell volumes and the reference volume are positive. The finite-species ideal chemical identity assumes positive amounts. Each site keeps its own elastic pressure law and fixed extra impermeant amount.
The donor and receiver have the same declared water compartment and initial reference volume. Species amounts and physical volume are read at the two endpoints of the event.

numerical.result: The copy stayed at 0.788048 pL, gained 1.1003 fmol of tracked osmoles and booked −0.138369 pJ of water free energy. The template changed both amount and volume at the other site. The largest combined energy discrepancy was 4.32 × 10⁻¹³ pJ against 2 × 10⁻¹¹ pJ. A three-step checked run reproduced both gross volume bookings.

biology.observable: Paired volume before removal and after arrival at the same site, with intracellular osmoles and mechanical or osmotic work.
biology.unit: pL per cell, µm³ per division, % of baseline volume and pJ per event

evidence.locator: Supplement page 4, panel marked S2L. Eleven line segments pair the mitotic parent with both daughters at the next frame.
evidence.context: Mouse basal epidermal cells were followed in vivo at 12-hour intervals. The register stores the paired figure readings in µm³.
evidence.uncertainty: The paired changes had a sample SD of 100 µm³. The authors report 9.1 ± 8.6% repeat-segmentation error overall. Imaging spans a full frame interval.
evidence.assessment: Mean volume was 770 µm³ for each parent and 677 µm³ for the sum of its daughters, with nine of eleven pairs decreasing. The paired change averaged −94 µm³. This measures division and leaves the same-site replacement volume and work open.

evidence.locator: Figure 1l and the accompanying results give the change in GFP-derived cytoplasmic volume.
evidence.context: MDCKII epithelial monolayers experienced a 20% hypertonic shock. Cells were grouped by subsequent extrusion or retention.
evidence.uncertainty: Values are mean ± SEM. The caption reports n = 5.
evidence.assessment: Cells subsequently extruded lost 20 ± 3% of baseline volume and retained cells lost 11 ± 2.5%. The assay measures outgoing shrinkage. Incoming absolute volume, osmole counts and work remain open.

claims.title: Centering a strictly interior replacement volume preserves its water-domain membership in exact arithmetic
claims.statement: For any declared target strictly between the water bounds, subtracting and adding the same reference volume recovers that target. The float64 implementation can refuse a strictly interior declaration when the reconstructed value lands on the excluded lower bound.
assumptions: The water volume interval is open at both endpoints. The exact theorem uses a common real-valued reference for storing and reconstructing the target.
The admission comparison uses a single template with the slot's own species amounts. Water flow is disabled and all other inputs are held fixed.

numerical.result: At reference 0.7505222518670602 pL the target 0.18763056296676509 pL reconstructs as the strict lower bound 0.18763056296676506 pL. Definition checking refuses the first interior float. The second interior float is admitted, as is the original target if only the lower bound is relaxed by one float.

biology.observable: Cell volume and measurement uncertainty near a physiologically justified lower bound. The recorded refusal concerns numerical admission.

claims.title: Size-triggered fission conserves each species under fixed-quota and independent partitions
claims.statement: Single-molecule growth and conservative division at the threshold cannot overshoot it. Ranking all occupied places selects exactly the declared quota. For a tracer species, fixed-quota sampling and independent per-molecule assignment give different probabilities of a tracer-free daughter, even when their mean allocations agree.
assumptions: Each molecule occupies one place and belongs to one species. The second daughter receives the complement. A split acts at the threshold before further growth.

The rank proof applies to any realized stable ordering and integer quota. The equal-subset probability assumes equiprobable rankings. The engine floors the float64 product of the fraction and the parent size.

For the binomial probabilities each molecule independently enters the named daughter with the same probability p. Comparing a center branch to two pooled side branches also assumes p is represented by the center volume fraction.

numerical.result: For a parent with two marked and two unmarked molecules, the named daughter had zero markers in 4 of 24 fixed-half rankings and 4 of 16 independent fair assignments. Padded places, ties and adjacent float64 quotas matched the specification. Exact weighted enumeration at parent counts 7, 9 and 12 matched the binomial variances at p = 1/3.

biology.observable: Variance of the center daughter's marked-particle count across divisions with a fixed reconstructed total.

evidence.locator: Figure 2c on printed page 031101-3. The pale-blue series gives the ultrasound-off control. Both side outlets are pooled.
evidence.context: Water droplets containing polystyrene beads split into three daughters of approximately equal volume. All 180 plotted control splits contribute to the empty-center comparison. The sample variances use reconstructed totals of 7, 9 and 12 beads.
evidence.uncertainty: At nine beads there are twelve plotted splits. The seven- and twelve-bead groups each contain seven splits. Counts were read from vector markers, including overlapping markers. Per-split volume fractions and raw paired counts are unavailable in the cited figure.
evidence.assessment: At nine beads the measured sample variance was 2.18, compared with 2.00 under independent assignment. At seven and twelve beads the measured values were 0.95 and 4.48, compared with 1.56 and 2.67. The 180 splits had zero empty centers. The nominal volume model gives a 26% probability of that outcome if splits are independent. The data leave independence and the engine’s size trigger unresolved.

claims.title: Switching an empty daughter pick to its sibling changes the sampled lineage
claims.statement: For a positive parent, the fallback always retains a nonempty daughter. When one daughter is empty, a fair initial pick retains the whole parent under fallback and half the parent on average if the initial pick stands. For either choice, the followed daughter’s log-weight jump equals minus the split work plus its sibling’s outgoing free energy.
assumptions: The initial choice and the partition are separate. The selection average gives each daughter label equal probability, then applies the declared empty-daughter policy.
An empty assembly has zero total molecules. A tracer-free daughter can still contain other species. Counts are measured at birth, before further chemical events.
A daughter at the size threshold divides again if its fission limit allows it. The signed work and sink use the assembly’s log weight with zero log weight for the empty state.

numerical.result: Across 32 equiprobable partition-and-pick outcomes for four molecules, fallback raised mean retained size from 2.00 to 2.25. At quota zero, selecting an empty daughter ended a lineage and following the full sibling gave five immediate re-splits before the limit. The every-descendant run recorded four empty and four full daughter births. The signed energy bookings matched the reference within 3.11 × 10⁻¹⁵ k_BT. The ledger docstring has a sign typo in its derivation.

biology.observable: Birth sizes and subsequent fates of both daughters, with the rule used to select the tracked daughter recorded for empty as well as occupied outcomes.
biology.finding: The bead experiment in the partition claim measures the cargo of a liquid droplet. Its center-versus-pooled-sides readout cannot identify an empty assembly or which sibling was followed. A direct measurement of this selection effect remains open.

claims.title: Serial transfer accounts for the spent bath and the vesicles removed
claims.statement: For each species, the new world plus the spent bath and removed vesicles contains the old world plus the fresh bath. Across consecutive washes, each slot retains its original cargo exactly when it is kept both times. The change in world free energy equals fresh-bath work minus the free energy exported.
assumptions: A transfer is instantaneous. It replaces the finite bath with declared counts and keeps each sampled vesicle intact. The proof conditions on the selected slots.
World free energy is the signed sum of the bath and individual live-vesicle free energies. Consecutive-wash composition assumes no intervening reaction or transport event.

numerical.result: Three compiled washes kept three of three, one of three, and one of one vesicles. All three species balanced exactly, including across two same-time schedules. The largest difference from independently calculated work, sink or world-energy change was 1.42 × 10⁻¹⁴ k_BT.

biology.observable: Tracer recovered in retained vesicles, the spent bath and removed vesicles across a wash, relative to the initial tracer and any fresh input.

evidence.citation: Fayolle et al. (2018), Table 1 and Fig. 3
evidence.locator: Table 1 reports three successive retentates. Figure 3A–E shows calcein fluorescence inside and outside vesicles.
evidence.context: Calcein-loaded DOPC/DOPA giant vesicles underwent successive dilution and microfiltration. The authors measured lipid in each retained fraction independently.
evidence.uncertainty: The signal ratios have a reported ±20% uncertainty. Later exterior signals reached the detector floor. The table gives no lipid error bars.
evidence.assessment: Exterior clearance raised the lumen-to-exterior signal ratio to 39, 89 and 137. Cumulative lipid recoveries were 40%, 26% and 16%. The individual tracer amounts in the retained and discarded fractions remain unresolved.

claims.title: Shear fission partitions the parent among all daughters and books discarded siblings
claims.statement: Assigning each molecule to one daughter preserves per-species inventories and the membrane footprint. If the total footprint cannot cover all daughter minima, every assignment fails. Shear work includes every daughter’s free energy. Following one daughter exports its siblings’ free energy.
assumptions: Counts are nonnegative integers, each molecule has one daughter, and each membrane species has a fixed footprint. The partition is evaluated before any daughter lysis.
The geometric admission formula assumes a nonnegative area and volume, a positive daughter count and consistent length units. The spherical capacity is computed from the available membrane area.
Each live daughter pays the same per-vesicle closure cost. The tracer signal comparison assumes a common linear calibration, zero background and no tracer leakage during the split.

numerical.result: Five accepted divisions conserved lipid and both solutes. Independent work and sibling-sink errors were at most 7.11 × 10⁻¹⁵ k_BT. Two parents below the combined daughter minimum stayed intact. The population stopped before drawing when its slots filled. Controls checked stress and volume refusals and 48 heterogeneous partitions.

biology.observable: Slope of the two daughters’ summed tracer signal against their parent’s signal in successful divisions.

evidence.locator: Figure 4a pairs total daughter and parent fluorescence for 78 divisions. The accompanying text describes the geometry and optical corrections.
evidence.context: DOPC-based giant liposomes divided at a microfluidic Y-junction. Each plotted parent produced two observable daughters.
evidence.uncertainty: The authors report slope 0.87 ± 0.01 (SD) and R² = 0.94. The estimated geometry and optical corrections approximately cancel.
evidence.assessment: The combined optical signal fell about 13% below perfect recovery. This disagrees with the conservative split under a common linear signal calibration. The escaped dye amount was not independently recovered.

claims.title: Lipid insertion scales with membrane area and diffusion-limited capture scales with radius
claims.statement: At fixed external number density, scaling the area-equivalent radius by s scales area-limited insertion by s² and diffusion-limited capture by s. A join and its reverse share the footprint before insertion. Their rate ratio is the exponential of reservoir work minus free-energy change in thermal units.
assumptions: The same species transfers between the pool and the bilayer. Each comparison holds its kinetic coefficient and external number density fixed.

The rate-ratio statement applies to an enabled two-way edge with a positive common coefficient, sufficient reactants and a defined discrete membrane counting measure. The endpoint energies include the declared excess terms.
The spherical diffusion-capture approximation uses the area-equivalent radius. The two encounter conventions describe different limiting mechanisms.

numerical.result: Doubling radius gave 4× area-limited insertion and 2× diffusion-limited capture. Across both transport steps, eight compiled configurations tested finite and held baths and both counting measures. All 40 blocked directions had zero rate. Across 64 active pairs the largest free-energy residual was 1.43 × 10⁻¹⁴ k_BT.

biology.observable: Lipid molecules inserted per vesicle per second at measured radius and matched free-monomer concentration, composition and temperature.

evidence.locator: Table 1 gives the PAzePC row. Equation 2 fits the area response.
evidence.context: Soluble PAzePC monomers at 0.5–1 µM were supplied to aspirated POPC vesicles under flow.
evidence.uncertainty: Mean ± SEM across 11 vesicles for the fitted PAzePC rates.
evidence.assessment: The measured association constant was 0.0027 ± 0.0005 µM⁻¹ s⁻¹. Release and movement between leaflets had separate rates. The pooled fractional area kinetics leave molecule flux by radius unresolved.

evidence.locator: Figure 2A plots initial filament elongation against starting vesicle diameter.
evidence.context: Multilamellar oleate vesicles grew under flow with 0.8 mM oleate micelles.
evidence.uncertainty: There is substantial scatter at each diameter. Filament width and free monomer concentration are additional uncertainties in a conversion to molecular flux.
evidence.assessment: Larger vesicles generally elongated faster. The authors could resolve neither a linear nor a quadratic dependence uniquely from this length readout.

claims.title: Neutral solute entry scales with area and spherical washout with inverse radius
claims.statement: The inward molecular rate equals permeability times area times outside number density. In an ideal lumen of fixed volume the exit rate per molecule is permeability times area divided by volume. On a sphere this predicts the first-order washout rate at a second radius from one calibration.
assumptions: External density and permeability are fixed for the forward-area comparison. A neutral molecule crosses between the bath and lumen without changing the footprint.

The outward concentration law assumes equal solution standard potentials, a well-mixed fixed volume and ideal solute with no extra energy change. A maintained solute-free exterior gives the exponential washout equation for the mean count.

For the liposome assay, use the study’s inner radius for both area and volume, a 4 nm bilayer thickness and a common permeability between sizes. The compiled readout is the initial exit rate divided by molecule count.

numerical.result: Doubling radius quadrupled molecular entry under both lipid-encounter conventions. The compiled exit rate per molecule at counts 1, 7 and 14 was 1.7500 s⁻¹ at the calibration radius and 1.2971 s⁻¹ at the second radius. All rate controls agreed with their independent calculations within 2 × 10⁻¹³ relative error.

biology.observable: Neutral-solute washout rate in fixed-size liposomes, and inward molecular uptake as a function of membrane area.

evidence.citation: Brändén et al. (2010), Fig. 3A and passive diffusion results
evidence.locator: Figure 3A and the accompanying results report the size-specific rates and the bilayer thickness.
evidence.context: Glycerol washed out of tethered POPC liposomes at 22 °C. Surface plasmon resonance tracked the change of internal concentration.
evidence.uncertainty: The smaller group reports ±0.02 s⁻¹ (n = 7). The 93 nm repeat has no published uncertainty or trace. Its exact concentration series is unspecified.
evidence.assessment: The larger liposomes emptied more slowly. Calibration at the smaller size underpredicts their rate by 0.163 s⁻¹. The uncertainty of the size transfer remains open.

evidence.locator: Three unarrowed traces in Figure 2a, from 20 to 80 s after each radius minimum.
evidence.context: Individual POPC vesicles stretched in the same 0.1 M urea bath. Swelling estimates net entry if water equilibrates rapidly and trapped sucrose is retained.
evidence.uncertainty: Moving either radius reading by ±0.10 µm gives ranges of 10.7–19.5, 15.9–32.1 and 25.6–47.3 fmol/s from smallest to largest. These describe figure resolution. Temperature and per-trace uncertainty were unreported.
evidence.assessment: For radii 31.80, 43.66 and 50.44 µm, inferred uptake was 15.1, 24.0 and 36.4 fmol/s. The largest/smallest uptake ratio was 2.41 and the compiled forward-area ratio was 2.52. The measured optical quantity was radius.

claims.title: Vesicles withdrawing from a finite shared bath conserve each species across the population
claims.statement: Each passive transfer changes one vesicle and the single bath by opposite integer counts. The inventory is conserved over every finite history of such transfers. Each live vesicle sees the same remaining bath density, and a permutation of the slots preserves the exact total rate.
assumptions: Follow one conserved species at a time with a finite common bath. The count proof covers passive uptake and release. Chemical conversion, fission, lysis, bath replacement and external supply need their own accounting.

A slot's uptake coefficient includes its own membrane geometry. The uptake-rate decrement in another slot assumes that slot's coefficient and the bath volume stay fixed. A relabelling carries occupancy and the full vesicle state together.

For the experimental area comparison, both populations start with equal lipid amounts and share an area per molecule. A 25% donor loss predicts a 25% recipient gain conditional on zero net change of free lipid in the bath.

numerical.result: Two 96-event osmotic populations conserved exactly one lipid and one solute across every stored row. All six slot permutations preserved the corresponding rates. The fixed-volume case failed during reporting. A parsed one-slot, one-event population raised TypeError when the reporter requested an osmotic volume for its declared lumen.

biology.observable: Paired changes in donor and recipient membrane area during passive competition, with independent measurement of material left in the common bath.

evidence.citation: Chen, Roberts and Szostak (2004), Figs. 1B and 1D
evidence.locator: Figures 1B and 1D and the accompanying 1:1 mixing result on page 1475.
evidence.context: Matched experiments label either the isotonic donor or the osmotically swollen recipient population of oleate vesicles.
evidence.uncertainty: Both area changes are approximate. Figure 1 gives no endpoint uncertainty. Fluorescence reports area and the free lipid pool was unmeasured.
evidence.assessment: The measured donor loss gives the conditional recipient gain shown. The experiment supports redistribution between populations. An empirical test of molecule closure still needs independent counts for donor, recipient and bath.

claims.title: Bilayer area is half the sum of the molecular footprints in its two leaflets
claims.statement: The integer footprint adds across lipid inventories. Refining the area unit preserves the physical area. A common per-lipid error bound gives a bilayer area bound of half the total lipid count times that error. The area-equivalent sphere gives the same volume from its radius and its area.
assumptions: Each membrane species has a fixed footprint expressed in integer quanta. Both leaflets contribute to the counted lipid inventory.
When the quantum is refined by a positive integer factor, every lipid’s integer weight and the integer floor scale by that factor. The physical quantum scales inversely.
The geometric reference is the sphere at the given area. A deflated vesicle can have a different shape and a smaller enclosed volume.

numerical.result: A 64-lipid control calibrated to fluid POPC at 30 °C gave 20.576 nm² and an empty lumen. In two compiled 96-event trajectories with different molecular weights for two lipids, every recorded integer footprint matched the independent count sum. A 32-fold refinement preserved the molecule counts across all 98 records.

biology.observable: Area per lipid at known composition and temperature, and total bilayer area in a vesicle with independently determined lipid counts.

evidence.locator: The POPC row at 30 °C supplies the per-lipid area. Equation 2 explains the uncertainty.
evidence.context: Fluid phosphatidylcholine bilayers characterized by joint small-angle neutron and X-ray scattering.
evidence.uncertainty: The reported uncertainty is ±0.013 nm² per lipid.
evidence.assessment: This calibrates the area of each lipid. An independent whole-vesicle check would require both its total lipid count and its measured membrane area.

claims.title: Membrane area caps the volume that minimizes a vesicle’s osmotic free energy
claims.statement: At fixed solute count, area and bath osmolarity, the equilibrium volume is the smaller of the ideal osmotic volume and the spherical volume allowed by the membrane. Tension vanishes below the cap. Once the cap is reached, further bath dilution raises tension while volume stays fixed.
assumptions: The bath is held, internal osmoles are conserved during equilibration, temperature is fixed, and water equilibrates rapidly. The minimum over positive volumes requires positive solute count, bath density, molecular standard and spherical capacity. The empty lumen is assigned zero volume and zero osmotic energy.
The membrane has fixed area within a bath comparison. Reduced volume divides by the spherical volume at that area. The ideal osmotic term uses particle density.

For the POPC transfer test, the first observation fixes the effective trapped solute per spherical volume. For the DOPC swelling transfer, the first group fixes a common volume reserve. The separate tension estimate uses an initially spherical inextensible membrane at the reported radius.

numerical.result: Two compiled trajectories each crossed between 34 slack and 64 tense records. Across both runs the relative volume error stayed below 1.07 × 10⁻¹⁴, tension error below 2.24 × 10⁻¹⁷ N/m, and osmotic energy error below 2.54 × 10⁻¹⁴ k_BT against a 70-digit reference. Separate 64-osmole worlds reproduce the macroscopic reduced-volume and tension-per-radius predictions at matched density.

biology.observable: Equilibrium volume after a bath osmolarity change, measured relative to the same vesicle’s spherical capacity or its initial volume, as specified for each study.

evidence.locator: Five paired osmolarity and reduced-volume labels printed below the confocal reconstructions.
evidence.context: One POPC vesicle weakly adhered by 0.4% PEG was tracked through sequential hypertonic bath changes. The prepared lumen contained 25 mM sucrose.
evaluation: 32, 46, 58 and 83 mOsm/L on the same vesicle
evidence.uncertainty: At 58 mOsm/L the label reads 0.30. Label rounding is ±0.005 and reported bath precision is ±2 mOsm/L. The paper gives no point-specific geometry uncertainty for Figure 2B.
evidence.assessment: The displayed pair is the 58 mOsm/L step after calibration at the first observation. All four later volumes were lower than predicted. Using prepared sucrose with no fit gave 0.431 at this step.

evidence.locator: The volume-increase measurements accompany Fig. 2B.
evidence.context: Micropipette-held giant DOPC vesicles were transferred from an isotonic 98 mM bath to 96 or 95 mM glucose. Volumes here are relative to each group’s initial volume.
evidence.uncertainty: Reported swelling was 1.7 ± 0.1% (14 vesicles) and 2.6 ± 0.1% (17 vesicles). The statistic for ±0.1 was unspecified. Transferring one area reserve across groups is an additional assumption.
evidence.assessment: The fixed-area model reaches its fitted limit at the first dilution and underestimates swelling at the second. An initially full sphere predicts zero swelling in both baths.

evidence.locator: Table 1 estimates the osmotic tension by matching rupture rates to isotonic aspiration controls.
evidence.context: A separate DOPC experiment at an initial osmotic difference of 1.9 mM and radius of 13.4 µm.
evidence.uncertainty: The reported osmotic tension was 2.6 ± 0.1 mN/m and initial radius 13.4 ± 0.2 µm. Tension was inferred from the rate measurements.
evidence.assessment: The initially spherical fixed-area model predicts 31.56 mN/m at that radius. Swelling and aspirated geometry limit this application of the spherical cap.

claims.title: Changing molecular area units preserves the exact vesicle rupture decision
claims.statement: When molecular areas and the physical floor are preserved, two choices of area quantum give identical physical area, capped volume, tension and strict rupture verdict for the same post-event counts. A vesicle that has survived a fixed threshold stays intact under that rule while every subsequent check sees no higher tension.
assumptions: Only the area unit and all associated integer weights and floor are rescaled. Solute count, temperature, bath, physical area and rupture threshold remain fixed.
The synthetic founder has five membrane lipids and four trapped osmoles. The only possible first event detaches one lipid. The comparison observes the outcome of that event.
The hold argument fixes each vesicle's threshold through time. The survival measurements track the same cohort after an applied tension is established.

numerical.result: The first event has reference tension 0.0008412963098275772 N/m. At thresholds about 3 × 10⁻¹⁸ N/m below and above it, the 60-quanta representation ruptured both times and the equivalent 1,920-quanta representation remained intact both times. Both matched the reference at thresholds 1% away. Computing physical area first recovered both close decisions in float64.

biology.observable: Intact fraction of a vesicle cohort over time at known tension. The numerical area-unit invariance is tested on identical physical states in the engine.

evidence.locator: Fig. 1a, open circles at 12 °C and open squares at 32 °C.
evidence.context: Pure DOPC giant unilamellar vesicles with matched sugar concentrations under a constant 8.0 mN/m aspiration tension. Time starts at the hold.
evidence.uncertainty: The published series reports 20 vesicles per temperature, but the plotted steps do not resolve those denominators. Fractions and times are approximate, and no pointwise errors are given.
evidence.assessment: At 12 °C survival fell from 0.50 at 92 s to 0.125 at 268 s. At 32 °C it fell from 0.50 at 33 s to 0.111 at 125 s. An instantaneous, fixed threshold acting alone cannot explain the continuing declines at constant tension.

evidence.locator: Open circles in Fig. 1B at the 4.3 mN/m aspiration setting. The results give n = 19.
evidence.context: Pure DOPC vesicles at 25 ± 1 °C with an initial osmolarity difference of 2.8 mM, followed after osmotic equilibration.
evidence.uncertainty: Two time points in the same cohort, read from the plotted steps. Fig. 1B has no pointwise error bars. Osmotic tension was inferred in addition to the applied aspiration tension.
evidence.assessment: Of 19 starting vesicles, 8 remained at 40 s and 2 at 110 s. Six of eight early survivors ruptured during the next 70 s. Any constant survival fraction misses at least one reading by 3/19, or 15.8 percentage points. The measured hold supplies no choice between numerical area quanta.

claims.title: Fluid from a held bath dilutes a growing cleft in proportion to its added volume
claims.statement: Filling a well-mixed cleft conserves solute. Its concentration stays between the original cleft and bath concentrations, and its excess above the bath scales with the retained volume fraction. Subdividing the fill gives the same endpoint. Dividing a facing patch between daughter cells preserves its total contribution to cleft volume.
assumptions: The cleft has positive initial volume. Added volume is nonnegative and arrives at the held bath concentration. The solute has no other source or sink during the fill.
Gap width stays fixed. The two daughter patches inherit the same fractions of current area and onset area, and replace the parent in the sum over live patches.
In the compiled comparison a neutral tracer is impermeant and face diffusion is zero. The account records the completed fill. The observer also includes the most recent half-step of membrane growth.

numerical.result: Five compiled controls checked all seven rows for volume, bath supply, tracer concentration and cumulative heat. When 0.010 pL at 4 mM grew to 0.020 pL from a 1 mM bath, both versions and a 60:40 patch split in version 2 gave 2.5 mM. The maximum concentration error was 4.45 × 10⁻¹⁶ mM.

biology.observable: Cleft width and bath access. A test of dilution during growth requires a paired cleft-volume and tracer-concentration time series.

evidence.citation: Spring and Hope (1979), Tables I and III
evidence.locator: Table I and pp. 291–292 give lateral area and assigned interspace volume. Table III gives pooled control volume per border length.
evidence.context: Live Necturus gallbladder epithelium in NaCl Ringer. The optically resolved area omits fine membrane folds.
fit: Resting lateral area and assigned interspace volume per cell
evidence.uncertainty: Area was 3,540 ± 150 µm² per cell (SEM, n = 32). Assigned interspace volume was about 2,080 µm³ per cell. Volume per border length was 41.1 ± 4.7 µm³/µm (SEM, n = 19).
evidence.assessment: The resting geometry gives an effective full gap width of 1.18 µm. The section-based estimate of 1.19 µm reuses the same images.

evidence.locator: Appendix 1, sections C.1–C.2, reports the layer width and size-dependent access.
evidence.context: Neighbouring cells in living CT26 spheroids. Confocal dye profiles measured width and bath tracers probed access to the extracellular matrix.
evidence.uncertainty: Reported width was 0.9 ± 0.1 µm across 132 profiles, with a correction for 0.27 µm optical resolution.
evidence.assessment: Tracers of 4.4 and 5.8 nm radius entered the space. Tracers above 14.8 nm were largely excluded. Access therefore depends on the solute.

evidence.locator: The abstract reports the result under the three bath and current conditions.
evidence.context: Ion-selective micropuncture of lateral spaces in Necturus gallbladder epithelium.
evidence.uncertainty: The authors report no reliable ion-concentration difference between lateral spaces and bath. A tracer-specific detection threshold and a mixing time are unavailable from this comparison.
evidence.assessment: Local ion measurements support bath-like concentrations under those conditions. Dilution during growth remains untested.

claims.title: Mixing two solutions of unequal positive concentration releases heat in the cleft
claims.statement: For each species in an ideal isothermal fill, mixing heat is the bath’s chemical and pressure work minus the cleft’s free-energy increase. Heat vanishes at equal concentration and is strictly positive for a positive addition of a different concentration. Both concentration ratios in the entropy formula remain positive.
assumptions: Initial volume, both concentrations and temperature are positive. The added bath volume is nonnegative. Strictly positive heat also requires positive added volume and unequal concentrations.
The comparison uses an isolated neutral tracer and a bath at 310 K. The energy reference evaluates the endpoint ideal-solution expression to 75 decimal digits.

numerical.result: At 1 and 2⁻⁶⁰ mM, in either orientation, the heat evaluator rounds one fractional deviation to −1 and produces NaN. Both versions refuse the first fill. The reference gives +0.00245660 or +0.00618054 pJ. Replacing only nonfinite heat with the direct positive-ratio form in memory lets all four complete, within 2.09 × 10⁻¹⁷ pJ of cumulative reference heat.

biology.observable: Heat released on mixing, with independently measured cleft and added volumes, solute concentrations and temperature. A local calorimetric measurement is still needed.

claims.title: A held bath can return to its original composition after supplying solute and work to tissue
claims.statement: Neutral formula units preserve bath charge. Across any sequence of solution changes, net controller dose and the bath’s ideal free-energy change depend only on the endpoints. The work delivered to tissue is the sum of the signed material supplied at each interval’s bath potential. A K-selective membrane at fixed intracellular K has a reversal shift set by the ratio of the two external K concentrations.
assumptions: The bath is held at fixed volume, temperature and electrical potential. Each formula unit has integer counts and zero net valence. Signed offsets specify absolute targets against the initial composition. Every resulting species concentration is positive.
Work is per species with positive supply into the tissue. The comparison uses ideal chemical potentials and the same held electrode potential before and after each switch.

For the voltage comparison K⁺ is the only permeant ion. Intracellular K activity stays fixed during the voltage scan and the ratio of external concentrations represents the activity ratio. The biological comparison uses differences between group means at steady bath levels.

numerical.result: Four neutral switches under ARS(2,2,2) and RK4 returned the bath’s net dose to zero, with 1.3955 × 10⁻⁴ fmol supplied to a finite pool. The work correction retained 2.5987 × 10⁻⁴ pJ. A separate 50-digit interval sum using each solver’s actual supply agreed within 5.43 × 10⁻²⁰ pJ at all 28 observations. The continuous finite-pool reference also checked the delivered amount. A compiled salt schedule reached all four experimental K concentrations.

biology.observable: Shift of the K-selective current reversal when extracellular KCl replaces NaCl in equal molar amounts. Local exchange time and the bath’s chemical work are separate observables.

evidence.citation: Randle, Oliet and Renaud (1991), p. 1796 and Fig. 3a
evidence.locator: Mean reversal potentials at 1, 2.5, 5.4 and 12 mM extracellular K⁺ from the Results. The Methods give equimolar NaCl replacement and 33–35 °C.
evidence.context: Whole-cell recordings in adult guinea-pig ventricular myocytes. Each endpoint is the reversal of the current induced by 100 µM cromakalim. The Cells comparison uses the midpoint temperature of 34 °C.
evaluation: All three adjacent concentration shifts, with no fitted voltages
evidence.uncertainty: At the four doses, reported means ± SEM were −131.5 ± 1.8, −104.6 ± 6.9, −87.2 ± 1.9 and −65.8 ± 2.2 mV. Clear reversals occurred in 4/9, 9/18, 12/14 and 7/9 recorded cells. The shifts compare group means. The temperature range gives +21.07 to +21.20 mV for 5.4 → 12 mM.
evidence.assessment: The displayed comparison is the 5.4 → 12 mM K⁺ step. For 1 → 2.5 and 2.5 → 5.4 mM the predicted shifts were +24.25 and +20.38 mV, against observed shifts of +26.9 and +17.4 mV. This checks the equilibrium membrane response. Bath exchange timing and reservoir work remain unmeasured in these cells.

claims.title: Permuting the formula units of a bath recipe preserves its exact dose
claims.statement: Each species’ target is the original amount plus the fixed bath volume times the signed sum of its contributions from the formula units. Permuting those contributions preserves the exact target, including a small residual after cancellation.
assumptions: The two definitions contain the same formula-unit counts, offsets, starting amount and bath volume. Only the order of the entries changes.

In the tests, the solute is neutral, the bath volume is 1 pL, and every input and count-times-offset product is exactly representable in float64. The independently calculated net dose is a binary fraction.

numerical.result: After the accurate-sum fix, both orders delivered the intended dose in all six checked worlds. Opposing contributions of ±24 mM preserved the 1.7763568394002505 × 10⁻¹⁵ fmol trace dose. The all-six-order regression passed. The earlier checkpoint records the ordering that erased the dose.

biology.observable: Independently assayed final solute concentration after preparing equivalent mixtures. Sensitivity to the order of entries in an engine input can be tested directly with the same recipe.

claims.title: A regulated channel approaches its held-dose plateau without overshoot
claims.statement: At fixed input a two-state gate stays in [0, 1] and moves toward its steady open fraction. Splitting a constant dose preserves its endpoint. For positive closing rate the rise time constant equals the zero-input washout time constant multiplied by one minus the plateau.
assumptions: The starting state lies in [0, 1]. During a half-step the opening rate a = k_on × input and the closing rate b are nonnegative and fixed. If both vanish, the state stays fixed. The time-constant relation requires b > 0 and complete removal of opening drive on washout.
An enabled route maps a factor f to basal + (1 − basal)f with basal in [0, 1]. The switch-off value is one. The upstream Hill ordering applies at positive concentration, half-saturation and exponent.

For the SK2 comparison the state is absolute open probability with zero basal opening. A single Hill input sets the opening rate, the closing rate is calcium-independent, and the single-channel and macropatch recordings share model parameters.

numerical.result: Six compiled pulse-and-washout runs agreed with the stage-by-stage state to 4.45 × 10⁻¹⁶. Against independent continuous integration the gate error fell from 7.41 × 10⁻⁴ to 1.83 × 10⁻⁴ and 4.55 × 10⁻⁵ as the step was halved. Both versions agreed on final channel availability and K⁺ transfer. Separate fixed-Ca²⁺ cells reproduced the calculated rise and washout time constants.

biology.observable: Absolute SK2 open probability at fixed free calcium and its relaxation time after calcium addition or removal.

evidence.locator: Figure 1B gives four single-channel steady doses. Figure 13A and its accompanying text give measured rapid calcium-jump kinetics.
evidence.context: Recombinant rat SK2 in excised Xenopus oocyte patches at nominal −80 mV. The four dose measurements came from one patch, and the jump kinetics from separate macropatches.
fit: Open probability at 0.6, 0.8 and 5 µM calcium
Mean washout time after 9.5 µM calcium
evaluation: Mean rise time after the jump to 9.5 µM calcium
evidence.uncertainty: Reading precision is about ±0.01 in absolute open probability. Shifting the three fitted points by that amount gave 0.543–0.589 at 1 µM and 9.76–11.34 ms for the rise across eight corner fits. The 5 µM solution shifted voltage by about 11 mV. Six jumps across two patches gave washout 57.3 ± 11.1 ms and rise 4.1 ± 0.6 ms (mean ± SD).
evidence.assessment: The held-out dose is from the same single-channel patch as the fitted doses. With its plateau and the independent macropatch washout mean, the one-state model predicts a 10.63 ms rise against 4.1 ± 0.6 ms measured. This tests whether one set of rates transfers between patches.

claims.title: Regulated turnover rates stay bounded and a changing regulator can give first-order production
claims.statement: A product of route factors in [0, 1] keeps the applied rate between zero and its scheduled maximum. When turnover produces its own regulator, taking a fresh Hill factor at the start of each target half-step can give first-order error in accumulated product.
assumptions: The scheduled rate is nonnegative. Each factor is evaluated in its declared range at the state received by the target half-step.

In the counterexample a fixed 1 pL cell starts at 1 mM regulator. The same turnover operator produces the regulator at 1 fmol/s and the reporter at a scheduled 1 fmol/s. Its reporter factor has zero basal activity, Hill exponent 1 and half-saturation 1 mM. Both routes are pure production.

Time is in seconds on [0, 1]. The target half-steps have uniform width h = dt/2 and an integer number spans the interval. The refinement bound compares accumulated gain on grids of width h and h/2 in exact arithmetic.

numerical.result: Version 2 reread the Hill factor in both target half-steps. All four ramp worlds accepted and booked their reporter gains. The exact one-second gain was 0.59453489 fmol. For 8, 16, 32 and 64 steps the measured convergence orders were 1.006, 1.003 and 1.002, failing the design’s second-order claim when turnover also changes the regulator. Lean proves that halving the target half-step increases this example’s gain by at least h/36.

biology.observable: An independently measured regulator concentration and absolute product appearance over time in the same well-mixed volume, with an independent calibration of the regulated production rate.

claims.title: Production and first-order clearance preserve a positive pool and account for gross turnover
claims.statement: At constant rates, the local pool solves dn/dt = P − kn. Production and clearance are separately nonnegative, their difference is the pool change, and subdivision preserves both the endpoint and the cumulative clearance. A balanced pool can have strictly positive production and clearance.
assumptions: The neutral species starts at a positive amount in a well-mixed node of fixed volume. Each schedule interval has nonnegative constant production P and first-order clearance k. Clearance rates for the same pool add. Only cells can have production in this operator.

The interval identities use exact real arithmetic. The numerical test also follows both gross bookings, the stored float64 amount and the signed chemical work when production and clearance are nearly equal.

The protein chase uses a signal proportional to the retained pulse-labeled cohort, with zero new labeled input and a constant clearance rate per protein. A second fit fixes the signal background to the measured control. The assay tests the decay curve and leaves the protein’s charge, molar amount and chemical work unmeasured.

numerical.result: 144 scalar cases per backend and two ordinary four-phase schedules matched the 60-digit reference. A one-second compiled run at extreme production and clearance accepted 1 fmol and zero work against a reference of 2 fmol and 0.995667 pJ. The two rounded gross bookings erased the net movement. Halving both rates recovered the correct result. A mixing-chamber check used metered input and exhaust without fitting the outlet measurements. At 120 minutes it predicted 0.387 vol% CO₂ against 0.318 ± 0.034 across four chambers (mean ± SD). [Riveros Lizana et al., Fig. 4](https://doi.org/10.3390/ani13162675)

biology.observable: Mean labeled-protein puncta per neuron after the label is removed. Absolute production and clearance of the total protein pool remain open.

evidence.citation: Dörrbaum et al. (2018), Figure 2B, source data 1
evidence.locator: GM130 and Lamin B1 counts for individual cells, including methionine-only background controls.
evidence.context: Primary rat hippocampal neurons after a two-hour pulse. Each protein’s day 0 signal sets its scale, and its day 1 signal sets its decay rate.
fit: Day 0 and day 1 for each protein
excluded: Unlabeled production and total protein amount
evidence.uncertainty: The displayed Lamin B1 day 7 mean is 11.62 ± 3.22 puncta per neuron (SD across 21 cells). The four late groups have 13–32 cells each. These SDs describe cell scatter. The holdouts are retrospective within one study.
evidence.assessment: For GM130 the early fit predicted 4.99 and 3.85 against means of 4.00 and 3.31 on days 2 and 3. For Lamin B1 it predicted 16.58 against 18.20 on day 3 and 5.07 against 11.62 on day 7. Including measured background raised the day 7 prediction to 5.97. The assay measures retention of labeled protein.

claims.title: Saturable uptake from a finite pool conserves neutral solute
claims.statement: The saturable import route has a unique positive remaining amount for every finite nonnegative dose. The receiving cell gains the amount removed. For two simultaneous routes with the same saturation concentration, each cell receives its capacity fraction of the shared pool’s depletion.
assumptions: Volume, patch area, saturation concentration and capacity stay fixed during each stage. The extracellular pool and its saturation amount are positive. The route moves a neutral species in one direction.
The Newton bracket and residual-to-amount bound use exact real arithmetic. The CPU comparison also checks how accurately the stored float64 amounts resolve a nearly depleted pool.
The continuous shared-pool allocation assumes the same K_M at both cells and no other sources, sinks or exchanges. The engine advances the two routes in a symmetric sequence.

numerical.result: 48 scalar cases per backend matched the independent reference. Six compiled two-cell runs conserved solute and reproduced the shared pool within 1.39 × 10⁻¹⁶ fmol. Halving the step reduced the cell allocation error by a factor of 4.01–4.06. At extreme depletion the 1 fmol anchor resolved a 6.31 × 10⁻¹⁶ fmol remainder to 5.65% and a smaller trial rounded to zero and was refused.

biology.observable: Initial neutral-solute uptake rate versus external concentration and a matched time course of extracellular depletion and intracellular gain.

evidence.locator: Filled circles for 3-O-methylglucose uptake into initially sugar-depleted erythrocytes.
evidence.context: Human red cells on ice, 30 s uptake. The reported rate scale is used directly. The preparation’s effective patch area and the rate’s volume denominator are unspecified.
evidence.uncertainty: The displayed 3 mM point is 117 ± 5 µmol/L/min (SE). Bars summarize three independent experiments in triplicate. The lowest-dose bar is unresolved. Estimated reading precision is ±1 µmol/L/min and ±0.02 mM.
evidence.assessment: The two-point calibration gave K_M = 1.19 mM. At 0.8, 1 and 3 mM the predicted rates were 60.7, 69.0 and 108.1 against 60 ± 4, 60 ± 8 and 117 ± 5. These comparisons test early uptake. Late depletion and two-cell allocation remain biologically open.

claims.title: Competing binding sites retain capacity through an SSPRK step
claims.statement: Each population keeps its total of free and bound sites. Both site counts stay nonnegative, and an initially positive shared ligand pool stays positive through the three-stage update.
assumptions: Free and bound counts start nonnegative and sum to capacity. Forward binding, release and internalisation have nonnegative rates.
At each stage the step length times every outgoing loss coefficient is at most one half. Populations drawing on the same ligand pool contribute to one summed coefficient.
The proof uses exact arithmetic and the SSPRK(3,3) weights. The comparison uses two populations at fixed volumes with one internalisation route.

numerical.result: In the finite-pool run both populations gained bound ligand. The largest ligand residual was 2.17 × 10⁻¹⁹ fmol and halving the step reduced the final ODE error by a factor of 8.26. Each route alone passed at load 0.300. Their combined loss load of 0.600 was refused.

biology.observable: Time-matched free ligand, occupancy of each of two competing site populations, and internalised cargo in a finite volume.

claims.title: Signed electrode pulses deliver the declared carrier charge
claims.statement: A pulse delivers the time-integrated current times the sum of the carrier fractions. For fractions summing to one this equals Ih at either polarity. On a single clamped patch the source books the change in chemical and capacitor energy less the clamp work.
assumptions: Current is constant over the interval h. Each active carrier has nonzero signed charge per fmol and the cell can supply every amount removed.

The tolerance theorem assumes the exact sum of the represented fractions is within the bound. The parser tests their floating-point sum. The one-patch energy identity assumes fixed capacitance and bath potential.
The physical comparison closes the background transport and uses an ideal solution at fixed cell volume.

numerical.result: Three carrier mixtures passed opposite 1 pA pulses. All material, charge and work ledgers matched the independent calculation. A fraction sum of 1.0000000005 delivered 2.000000001 fC for a nominal 2 fC.

biology.observable: Calibrated delivered current, the carrier-specific supply and removal, and clamp work on the same cell and pulse interval.

claims.title: Three passive ions set one zero-current membrane voltage
claims.statement: For monovalent Na⁺, K⁺ and Cl⁻ the analytic sum of the outward constant-field currents vanishes exactly at the Goldman–Hodgkin–Katz voltage. The chloride concentrations enter in the opposite order to sodium and potassium.
assumptions: The concentrations, effective permeabilities and temperature are fixed during the voltage comparison, the thermal voltage RT/F is positive and both permeability-weighted concentration sums are positive.

The membrane carries only these three passive ions. The analytic identity agrees with the engine’s real-arithmetic evaluator at zero and outside its near-zero series interval. We also compare float64 at one nonzero reversal inside that interval.

numerical.result: Four roots of the Cells membrane current matched the analytic voltage within 2 × 10⁻¹⁵ V. At −47.168248 mV, outward Na, K and Cl currents were −0.557437, +0.491856 and +0.065581 pA. All three also matched on both sides of reversal and in a two-step run.

biology.observable: Resting voltage shifts under known ion substitutions and separate currents for each ion at the same reversal.

evidence.locator: Resting rows B, C and E in the original printed table.
evidence.context: Resting squid giant axon in two potassium-enriched artificial seawater solutions and one diluted seawater solution. Shifts use inside-minus-outside voltage.
fit: Published resting permeability ratios chosen using the experimental series
evaluation: Three resting shifts against the appropriate baseline bath
excluded: Action potential, afterpotential and individual ionic currents
evidence.uncertainty: Table 7 gives means rounded to mV without row-specific uncertainties. The calculation adopts 21 °C from Table 3.
evidence.assessment: For B, C and E, observed shifts were +2, +4 and −2 mV. The reconstructed Cells shifts were +2.10, +4.03 and −1.58 mV. The displayed pair is solution C. The three ionic currents were unmeasured.

claims.title: Reversing a junction reverses its flux
claims.statement: Exchanging the concentrations at the two ends of a constant-field junction and reversing the voltage difference negates the signed flux.
assumptions: The ion, temperature, area, permeability and opening are the same in both orientations. Voltage is sender potential minus receiver potential, scaled by zF/(RT).
The proof treats both the analytic Bernoulli factor and the engine’s near-zero series in real arithmetic. A floating-point error bound for the series remains open.

numerical.result: The CPU surface tests exercised reversed routes, multiple patches and padding against the independent flux reference.

biology.observable: Signed transfer rate of the same ion in a cell pair with the endpoint conditions exchanged.
biology.finding: A single Cx43 channel carried about −5 pA at −50 mV and +4.8 to +4.95 pA at +50 mV in symmetric salt. This checks reversal of electrical current. Reversal of one ion’s flux under exchanged concentrations remains open. [Wang and Veenstra, Fig. 1](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9101407/)

claims.title: At equal voltage, junction flux follows the concentration gradient
claims.statement: At equal potentials the signed flux is scale × (sender concentration − receiver concentration). A positive scale gives flow from higher to lower concentration.
assumptions: The transport factor has value one at zero voltage. The scale is area × permeability × opening divided by mol/fmol. The direction claim requires a positive scale.

numerical.result: The equal-voltage CPU fixture exercised concentration differences of both signs and compared the signed flux with an independent scalar calculation.

biology.observable: Ion transfer across a junction at equal potentials and a measured concentration difference.
biology.finding: Near zero junction voltage, a charged tracer moved from the loaded cell to its neighbor. A separate study estimated 226 ± 75 calcein molecules/s per Cx26 channel at a 125 μM gradient, with only the donor voltage-clamped during transfer.
